D.t: Deb Haaland leads by 11.6 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 94,230 votes; a one point swing is about 4,065 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +4.3 and D +18.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +6.7. Your best recent poll is Research Co. at D +8.0; your worst is SurveyUSA at D +5.4. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Bernalillo, a projected net 65,735 votes; Santa Fe, a projected net 42,931 votes; Doña Ana, a projected net 13,382 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sandoval, D +4.5, 8.4% of the vote; Cibola, D +8.8, 1.0% of the vote; Socorro, D +6.0, 0.8% of the vote; Colfax, R +6.7, 0.6% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Deb Haaland runs furthest behind in Sandoval, Los Alamos, Bernalillo. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 57 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 63% of voters, 58 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.15 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 55 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.00 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Deb Haaland: Immigration voters 29 to 71, Small counties 47 to 53, White voters 50 to 50. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.8M cash against $520K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 51% of the 450,949 ballots in New Mexico so far, against 31% for the other party. That is 1.5 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points away from Deb Haaland. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Early vote: Registered Republicans cast 31% of the 450,949 ballots in New Mexico so far, against 51% for the other party.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: San Juan, a projected net 10,945 votes; Lea, a projected net 10,193 votes; Eddy, a projected net 9,296 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sandoval, D +4.5, 8.4% of the vote; Cibola, D +8.8, 1.0% of the vote; Socorro, D +6.0, 0.8% of the vote; Colfax, R +6.7, 0.6% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Gregg Hull runs furthest behind in McKinley, Grant, San Miguel. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 43 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 63% of voters, 42 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.15 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 45 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.00 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Gregg Hull: Corruption voters 30 to 70, Health care and Social Security voters 30 to 70, Independents 34 to 66. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
